name: harmonium

entries.name: Stack
entries.description: Lays out items in a column (or a row with `direction="horizontal"`) with consistent gaps. Props take a single value or a responsive object (`{base: 'vertical', md: 'horizontal'}`).

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of items on the cross axis

props.name: justify
props.description: Justification of items on the main axis

entries.name: Group
entries.description: Lays out items in a row. Props take a single value or a responsive object (`{base: true, md: false}`).

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of items on the cross axis

props.name: justify
props.description: Justification of items on the main axis

props.name: grow
props.description: Whether every item grows to share the row's width equally (`flex: 1`)

entries.name: Grid
entries.description: A CSS grid. `columns` is a count (`12` means 12 equal columns) or any `grid-template-columns` value; place children in `GridCol`s. Props take a single value or a responsive object (`{base: 1, md: 2, lg: 3}`).
examples:
```tsx
<Grid columns={12} gap="md">
  <GridCol span={{base: 12, md: 4}}>Sidebar</GridCol>
  <GridCol span={{base: 12, md: 8}}>Content</GridCol>
</Grid>
```

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of items within their grid area

entries.name: GridCol
entries.description: A `Grid` cell. `span` is a column count, or any `grid-column` value (`'1 / -1'`).

entries.name: Separator
entries.description: A horizontal or vertical divider (`<hr>`).

entries.name: Container
entries.description: Centers content with a max width and horizontal padding. Both props take a single value or a responsive object (`{base: 'md', lg: 'xl'}`).

entries.name: AppShell
entries.description: Page layout grid with header, sidebar, main and footer areas. `sidebarCollapsed` narrows the sidebar column to 60px; below 768px the areas stack.

entries.name: AppShellHeader
entries.description: The `AppShell` header area, a `<header>`.

entries.name: AppShellSidebar
entries.description: The `AppShell` sidebar column, an `<aside>`.

entries.name: AppShellMain
entries.description: The `AppShell` main content area, a `<main>`.

entries.name: AppShellFooter
entries.description: The `AppShell` footer area, a `<footer>`.

entries.name: Sidebar
entries.description: Side navigation: a `<nav>` of `SidebarSection`s and `SidebarItem`s. When `collapsed`, items show only their icons and keep their label as their accessible name. Give it an `aria-label` when the page has more than one `<nav>`.
examples:
```tsx
<Sidebar aria-label="Main" collapsed={collapsed}>
  <SidebarSection label="Workspace">
    <SidebarItem icon={<HomeIcon />} href="/" active>Home</SidebarItem>
    <SidebarItem icon={<GearIcon />} render={<Link to="/settings" />}>Settings</SidebarItem>
  </SidebarSection>
</Sidebar>
```

props.name: collapsed
props.description: Whether the sidebar is collapsed to icon-only mode

entries.name: SidebarSection
entries.description: A group of `SidebarItem`s, optionally labelled.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional label for the section. Also names the section as a group.

entries.name: SidebarItem
entries.description: A navigation item: a `<button>`, an `<a>` with `href`, or your router link with `render`. `active` marks the current page. A disabled item can't be focused or followed.

props.name: active
props.description: Whether this item is the current page. Sets `aria-current="page"`.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon element rendered before the label

props.name: href
props.description: Link target. When set, the item renders as an `<a>` instead of a `<button>`.

props.name: render
props.description: Replaces the rendered element, e.g. a router link: `render={<Link to="/settings" />}`. Harmonium's props (class, data attributes, ARIA) are merged onto it.

entries.name: Show
entries.description: Shows its children only at some screen widths, using the `breakpoints` (sm 640px, md 768px, lg 1024px, xl 1280px). It hides them with CSS, so they are still rendered.

props.name: above
props.description: Show content at this breakpoint and above

props.name: below
props.description: Show content below this breakpoint (hidden at and above)

entries.name: Text
entries.description:
Body text with size, weight and color variants. Renders a `

` unless `as` says otherwise.
examples:
```tsx
<Text>Your trial ends in 3 days.</Text>
<Text size="sm" color="muted" as="span">Updated 2 hours ago</Text>
```

props.name: truncate
props.description: Whether to truncate overflow with ellipsis

props.name: htmlFor
props.description: Id of the labelled control (only used when `as="label"`)

entries.name: Heading
entries.description: A heading. `level` sets the element (`h1`–`h6`, default `h2`) and `size` the look, so the outline and the styling can differ.

entries.name: Field
entries.description: Groups a form control with its label, description and error, and wires them up for assistive technology: `FieldLabel`'s `htmlFor` points at the control, and the control's `aria-describedby` lists the description and error that are rendered. `error` marks the control `aria-invalid`.
examples:
```tsx
<Field error={!!errors.email}>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <FieldDescription>We'll never share it.</FieldDescription>
  <Input type="email" name="email" />
  <FieldError>{errors.email}</FieldError>
</Field>
```

props.name: error
props.description: Whether the field has an error

entries.name: FieldLabel
entries.description: The `<label>` of a `Field`, pointed at its control.

entries.name: FieldDescription
entries.description: Help text for a `Field`, linked to its control with `aria-describedby`.

entries.name: FieldError
entries.description: A `Field`'s error message (`role="alert"`), linked to its control with `aria-describedby` and `aria-errormessage`. It renders nothing while empty.

props.name: match
props.description: When to show the message. By default it shows whenever it has content, so `<FieldError>{errors.email}</FieldError>` renders nothing while there is no error. Without children it shows the browser's validation message once the control is invalid. Pass a `ValidityState` key (e.g. `"valueMissing"`) to show it only for that failure.

entries.name: useFieldContext
entries.description: Reads the surrounding `<Field>`, or `null` outside one. Use it to build your own Field-aware control: put `fieldId` on the control, `describedBy` in its `aria-describedby` and `error` in its `aria-invalid`. Harmonium's own controls are wired up automatically.

entries.name: FieldContextValue
entries.description: What `useFieldContext()` returns inside a `Field`.

props.name: fieldId
props.description: The id the Field gives its control (and the `htmlFor` of `FieldLabel`). A Harmonium control given its own `id` keeps it, and `FieldLabel` follows that id instead.

props.name: error
props.description: Whether the field has an error

props.name: labelId
props.description: The id of the `FieldLabel` (its own `id` when you pass one)

props.name: descriptionId
props.description: The id of the `FieldDescription`, when one is rendered (its own `id` when you pass one)

props.name: errorId
props.description: The id of the `FieldError`, when one is rendered (its own `id` when you pass one)

props.name: describedBy
props.description: Space-separated ids of the description and error parts that are actually rendered, ready for `aria-describedby`. `undefined` when there are none.

entries.name: Input
entries.description: A native `<input>`. Inside a `<Field>` it is labelled by `FieldLabel`, described by `FieldDescription`/`FieldError` and marked invalid by `<Field error>` (via Base UI's `Field.Control`).
examples:
```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Name</FieldLabel>
  <Input value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
</Field>
<Input type="search" size="sm" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
```

entries.name: Textarea
entries.description: A native `<textarea>`, wired to the surrounding `<Field>`.
examples:
```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Bio</FieldLabel>
  <FieldDescription>A sentence or two about you.</FieldDescription>
  <Textarea rows={4} value={bio} onChange={(e) => setBio(e.target.value)} />
</Field>
```

entries.name: Select
entries.description: A native `<select>`, wired to the surrounding `<Field>`. Pass `<option>` elements as children.
examples:
```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Role</FieldLabel>
  <Select placeholder="Choose a role" value={role} onChange={(e) => setRole(e.target.value)}>
    <option value="admin">Admin</option>
    <option value="member">Member</option>
  </Select>
</Field>
```

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder option text. It is shown (and submits an empty value) until an option is picked, in both controlled and uncontrolled use.

entries.name: Checkbox
entries.description:
A checkbox with a label.

Built on Base UI's Checkbox: a `<span role="checkbox">` (the visible box, `.indicator`) plus a hidden native input that carries `name`/`value` for form submission.

Prop routing: `className` and `style` go on the wrapping `<label>` (the visible component); `ref` points at the hidden `<input type="checkbox">`; `onChange` receives that input's change event; everything else (`aria-*`, `data-*`, `onFocus`, ...) goes on the `role="checkbox"` element.
examples:
```tsx
<Checkbox label="Remember me" name="remember" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="I agree" checked={agreed} onChange={(e) => setAgreed(e.target.checked)} />
```

entries.name: Radio
entries.description:
A radio button with a label, used inside a `RadioGroup`.

Inside a `RadioGroup` it is Base UI's Radio: a `<span role="radio">` (the `.indicator`) plus a hidden native input that carries `name`/`value` for form submission. Outside a group it falls back to a plain native radio.

Prop routing: `className` and `style` go on the wrapping `<label>`; `ref` points at the native `<input type="radio">`; `onChange` receives that input's change event; `name`, `checked` and `defaultChecked` are read by the group; everything else goes on the `role="radio"` element.
examples:
```tsx
<RadioGroup legend="Plan" name="plan" value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>
```

entries.name: RadioGroup
entries.description:
A group of `Radio`s with a `legend`; one can be selected.

Built on Base UI's RadioGroup: a `<fieldset role="radiogroup">` with roving focus and arrow-key selection. The `name` for form submission comes from the group, or from the radios' `name`.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected value (controlled). Alternatively set `checked` on a `Radio`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initially selected value. Alternatively set `defaultChecked` on a `Radio`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the newly selected value

props.name: required
props.description: Whether a selection is required to submit the form

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the selection can't be changed

entries.name: Switch
entries.description:
An on/off switch with a label.

Built on Base UI's Switch: a `<span role="switch">` (the `.track`) with a `.thumb`, plus a hidden native checkbox that carries `name`/`value` for form submission.

Prop routing: `className` and `style` go on the wrapping `<label>` (the visible component); `ref` points at the hidden `<input type="checkbox">`; `onChange` receives that input's change event; everything else (`aria-*`, `data-*`, `onFocus`, ...) goes on the `role="switch"` element.
examples:
```tsx
<Switch label="Email notifications" checked={enabled} onChange={(e) => setEnabled(e.target.checked)} />
<Switch label="Dark mode" size="sm" defaultChecked />
```

entries.name: Slider
entries.description:
A range slider; `showValue` shows the current value next to it.

Built on Base UI's Slider. Keyboard, pointer and screen-reader support come from Base UI; a visually hidden `<input type="range">` inside the thumb carries `name`/`value` for form submission.

Prop routing: `ref`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-valuetext`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onKeyDown` and `tabIndex` go to that range input; `onChange` receives a change event whose `target` is that input; `className`, `style`, `id` and other attributes go on the root `<div>`.
examples:
```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Volume</FieldLabel>
  <Slider min={0} max={100} value={volume} onChange={(e) => setVolume(Number(e.target.value))} showValue />
</Field>
```

props.name: showValue
props.description: Whether to show the current value label

entries.name: NumberInput
entries.description:
A number input with decrement and increment buttons. Arrow keys step by `step`; typed values are clamped to `min`/`max` on blur or Enter.

Built on Base UI's NumberField. The visible input is a text field with `role="spinbutton"`; a hidden `<input type="number">` carries `name`/`value` for form submission.

Prop routing: `className` goes on the root `<div>`; `id`, `name`, `form`, `disabled`, `readOnly` and `required` configure the field (and reach the stepper buttons); `ref` and every other attribute go on the visible input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Change handler. Called with finite numbers only: while typing it gets the typed number as-is; out-of-range values are clamped to `min`/`max` when the input loses focus or Enter is pressed. Clearing the input doesn't call it.

props.name: decrementLabel
props.description: Accessible label of the decrement button

props.name: incrementLabel
props.description: Accessible label of the increment button

entries.name: Combobox
entries.description: A searchable single-select: typing filters `options`, arrow keys move through them and Enter picks one. Follows the ARIA combobox pattern. Controlled with `value` + `onChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. Wired to the surrounding `Field`.
examples:
```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Country</FieldLabel>
  <Combobox
    options={[{value: 'us', label: 'United States'}, {value: 'ca', label: 'Canada'}]}
    value={country}
    onChange={setCountry}
    placeholder="Search countries"
  />
</Field>
```

props.name: value
props.description: Current value (controlled). Use `''` for no selection.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback when value changes. Receives `''` when the input is cleared.

entries.name: ComboboxOption
entries.description: An option of a `Combobox`.

props.name: value
props.description: Value passed to `onChange` when this option is chosen

props.name: label
props.description: Text shown in the list and in the input, and matched by search

entries.name: DatePicker
entries.description: A native `<input type="date">`, wired to the surrounding `<Field>`. Its value is an ISO date string (`'2026-10-11'`).

entries.name: TimePicker
entries.description: A native `<input type="time">`, wired to the surrounding `<Field>`. Its value is a 24-hour `HH:mm` string.

entries.name: FileUpload
entries.description: A drop zone that also opens the file picker on click, Enter or Space. Picked and dropped files are checked against `accept`, `maxSize` and `multiple`: matching files go to `onChange`, the rest to `onReject`. It doesn't upload anything itself. Children replace the default "Drop files here or click to browse" text.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether multiple files can be selected

props.name: onReject
props.description: Callback with the files left out for not matching `accept`, `maxSize` or `multiple`

entries.name: MultiSelect
entries.description: A searchable multi-select. Selected options show as removable tags (Backspace removes the last one); typing filters the list. Follows the ARIA combobox pattern. Controlled with `value` + `onChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. Wired to the surrounding `Field`.

entries.name: MultiSelectOption
entries.description: An option of a `MultiSelect`.

props.name: value
props.description: Value included in `onChange`'s array when selected

props.name: label
props.description: Text shown in the list and on the selected tag, and matched by search

entries.name: Button
entries.description: A native `<button>` with variants and sizes.
examples:
```tsx
<Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>
<Button variant="outline" disabled>Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Edit</Button>
<Button expanded>Full width</Button>
```

props.name: expanded
props.description: Whether the button should take full width

entries.name: ToggleGroup
entries.description:
A set of toggle buttons where one is selected, like a segmented control.

Built on Base UI: the group is one tab stop, arrow keys (and Home/End) move focus between items, and each item reports its state with `aria-pressed`. Pressing the selected item again keeps it selected. Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback when the selected value changes

entries.name: ToggleGroupItem
entries.description: A toggle button in a `ToggleGroup`, pressed while its `value` is selected.

entries.name: Card
entries.description: A content container, with optional `CardHeader`, `CardBody` and `CardFooter` sections.
examples:
```tsx
<Card variant="outlined">
  <CardHeader>Plan</CardHeader>
  <CardBody>You're on the free plan.</CardBody>
  <CardFooter><Button size="sm">Upgrade</Button></CardFooter>
</Card>
```

entries.name: CardHeader
entries.description: The top section of a `Card`, usually its title.

entries.name: CardBody
entries.description: The main content of a `Card`.

entries.name: CardFooter
entries.description: The bottom section of a `Card`, usually actions.

entries.name: Badge
entries.description: A short status label.

entries.name: Alert
entries.description: A message banner. `info` and `success` use `role="status"` (announced politely); `warning` and `error` use `role="alert"`. With `dismissible` it shows a "Dismiss" button that calls `onDismiss`; removing the alert is up to you.
examples:
```tsx
<Alert variant="success">Your changes were saved.</Alert>
<Alert variant="error" dismissible onDismiss={() => setError(null)}>
  Couldn't save your changes.
</Alert>
```

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Whether the alert can be dismissed

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Callback when the alert is dismissed

entries.name: Progress
entries.description: A progress bar (`role="progressbar"`). `showLabel` adds the percentage below the bar.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Whether to show the value label

entries.name: Spinner
entries.description: A loading indicator, announced as `role="status"` with `label`.

entries.name: Avatar
entries.description: A user's picture, or `fallback` text (usually initials) when there's no `src` or the image fails to load. The fallback is announced as an image named by `alt`, else `fallback`.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Fallback text (typically initials) shown when no image

entries.name: Skeleton
entries.description: A pulsing placeholder shown while content loads. Numbers for `width` and `height` are pixels. The pulse stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

entries.name: Tag
entries.description: A label for a category, filter or selection. With `removable` it shows a remove button named "Remove <label>" that calls `onRemove`.

props.name: removable
props.description: Whether the tag can be removed

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback when the remove button is clicked

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon or avatar rendered before the label

entries.name: EmptyState
entries.description: A placeholder for when there's nothing to show yet: icon, title, description and an action.
examples:
```tsx
<EmptyState
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Create a project to get started."
  action={<Button onClick={create}>New project</Button>}
/>
```

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon or illustration displayed above the title

props.name: action
props.description: Action element (typically a Button) displayed below the description

entries.name: Stat
entries.description: A key metric: label, value and an optional change colored by `trend`.
examples:
```tsx
<Grid columns={{base: 1, md: 3}} gap="md">
  <Stat label="Revenue" value="$48,200" change="+12%" trend="up" />
  <Stat label="Churn" value="2.1%" change="-0.4%" trend="down" />
</Grid>
```

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon or sparkline rendered alongside the value

entries.name: Tabs
entries.description:
Tabbed panels: one `TabsContent` shows at a time.

Built on Base UI: arrow keys (and Home/End) move between tabs with a roving tabindex, and each tab is wired to its panel with `aria-controls` / `aria-labelledby`. Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`.
examples:
```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="profile">
  <TabsList aria-label="Settings">
    <TabsTrigger value="profile">Profile</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="billing">Billing</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="profile">…</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="billing">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Default active tab ID (uncontrolled). When omitted, the first enabled tab is selected.

entries.name: TabsList
entries.description: The row of `TabsTrigger`s (`role="tablist"`).

entries.name: TabsTrigger
entries.description: A tab (`role="tab"`) that shows the `TabsContent` with the same `value`.

entries.name: TabsContent
entries.description: The panel (`role="tabpanel"`) shown while its tab is active.

props.name: value
props.description: Tab ID this content belongs to

entries.name: Accordion
entries.description: Expandable sections. One item opens at a time unless `multiple`. Each trigger sits in an `<h3>`, toggles `aria-expanded` and controls a labelled `region` panel. Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`.
examples:
```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue="shipping">
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionTrigger value="shipping">Shipping</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent value="shipping">Ships in 2 days.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="returns">
    <AccordionTrigger value="returns">Returns</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent value="returns">30-day returns.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allow multiple items to be open simultaneously

entries.name: AccordionItem
entries.description: One section of an `Accordion`: wraps its `AccordionTrigger` and `AccordionContent`.

entries.name: AccordionTrigger
entries.description: The button that opens and closes its `AccordionItem`, rendered inside an `<h3>` heading. `ref`, `className` and other props go to the button.

props.name: value
props.description: Item value this trigger controls (the enclosing `AccordionItem` decides)

entries.name: AccordionContent
entries.description: The collapsible panel of an `AccordionItem`, labelled by its trigger.

props.name: value
props.description: Item value this content belongs to (the enclosing `AccordionItem` decides)

entries.name: Breadcrumbs
entries.description: A breadcrumb trail: a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` with an ordered list of `BreadcrumbItem`s and a decorative separator between them.

entries.name: BreadcrumbItem
entries.description: One breadcrumb: a link, or with `active` the current page, rendered as a `<span aria-current="page">` without the link attributes.

props.name: active
props.description: Whether this is the current/active page

entries.name: Pagination
entries.description: Previous/next buttons and page numbers. Shows at most `maxVisible` page buttons, always including the first and last page, with an ellipsis for skipped pages. It's controlled: update `page` in `onPageChange`.

props.name: maxVisible
props.description: Maximum number of visible page buttons

entries.name: TopBar
entries.description: An application header bar (`<header>`) with `TopBarSection`s aligned left, center or right. `fixed` pins it to the top of the viewport.

props.name: fixed
props.description: Whether the TopBar is fixed to the top

entries.name: TopBarSection
entries.description: A group of items in a `TopBar`, aligned with `align`.

entries.name: Table
entries.description: A semantic HTML table built from `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableRow`, `TableHeader` (`<th>`) and `TableCell` (`<td>`). For column definitions and sorting, use `DataGrid`.

props.name: striped
props.description: Whether to apply striped row styling

props.name: hoverable
props.description: Whether to apply hover styling to rows

props.name: responsive
props.description: Whether the table should scroll horizontally. When it overflows, the scroll container becomes keyboard focusable and, if the table has an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`, a region with the same name.

entries.name: TableHead
entries.description: The `<thead>` of a `Table`.

entries.name: TableBody
entries.description: The `<tbody>` of a `Table`.

entries.name: TableRow
entries.description: A `<tr>` of a `Table`.

entries.name: TableHeader
entries.description: A header cell (`<th>`) of a `Table`.

entries.name: TableCell
entries.description: A data cell (`<td>`) of a `Table`.

entries.name: DataGrid
entries.description: A table driven by `columns` and `data`. Clicking a `sortable` header cycles ascending, descending, unsorted. Without `sort`, DataGrid sorts `data` itself (by `row[key]`, or the column's `sortValue`; empty values last). With `sort`, it's controlled: rows render in the order you pass, so sort `data` in `onSortChange`. When the grid overflows, its scroll area is keyboard focusable. `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` name the `<table>`.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Function to get a unique key for each row

props.name: sort
props.description: Current sort state (controlled). When set, `data` is rendered in the order given; sort it yourself in `onSortChange`. Leave it out to let DataGrid sort `data` itself.

props.name: tableProps
props.description: Extra props for the `<table>` element (the outer `<div>` gets the rest)

entries.name: DataGridColumn
entries.description: A column of a `DataGrid`.

props.name: sortValue
props.description: Value to sort by when DataGrid sorts `data` itself (uncontrolled sorting). Defaults to `row[key]`.

entries.name: SortState
entries.description: The sorted column and direction of a `DataGrid`.

entries.name: SortDirection
entries.description: A sort direction; `null` means unsorted.

entries.name: Dialog
entries.description: A modal dialog, rendered in a portal on `document.body`. While open it traps focus, locks page scroll and returns focus on close. It's controlled: it calls `onClose` on Escape or a backdrop click, and you set `open` to false. A `DialogHeader` inside labels it. It has no built-in close button.
examples:
```tsx
<Dialog open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} size="sm">
  <DialogHeader>Delete project?</DialogHeader>
  <DialogBody>This can't be undone.</DialogBody>
  <DialogFooter>
    <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button onClick={remove}>Delete</Button>
  </DialogFooter>
</Dialog>
```

props.name: onClose
props.description: Callback when the dialog should close

entries.name: DialogHeader
entries.description: The title area of a `Dialog`. Inside a Dialog or Drawer, it also labels the dialog (`aria-labelledby`).

entries.name: DialogBody
entries.description: The main content of a `Dialog` or `Drawer`.

entries.name: DialogFooter
entries.description: The actions row at the bottom of a `Dialog` or `Drawer`.

entries.name: Drawer
entries.description: A modal panel that slides in from the left or right edge. It behaves like `Dialog` (portal, focus trap, scroll lock, `onClose` on Escape or a backdrop click) and can hold `DialogHeader`, `DialogBody` and `DialogFooter`.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Callback when the drawer should close

props.name: side
props.description: Side the drawer slides in from

entries.name: Tooltip
entries.description: A short description shown when its child is hovered or focused. The child must be focusable (for example a `Button`); it gets `aria-describedby` pointing at the tooltip, merged with any it already has. Closes on Escape.

props.name: side
props.description: Side of the trigger to show the tooltip

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds to wait before showing the tooltip on hover (focus shows it immediately)

entries.name: Popover
entries.description: Floating content that opens when its child is clicked. The child (for example a `Button`) becomes the trigger. The popup is portalled, flips when there's no room, and closes on Escape or an outside click, returning focus to the trigger. Uncontrolled by default, or controlled with `open` + `onOpenChange`.

props.name: side
props.description: Side of the trigger to show the popover

entries.name: Menu
entries.description: A list of actions. With `trigger` it's a dropdown that opens from that element; without it, it renders inline. Either way it has one tab stop, arrow keys, Home/End and typeahead, and skips disabled items.
examples:
```tsx
<Menu trigger={<Button variant="outline">Actions</Button>}>
  <MenuLabel>Project</MenuLabel>
  <MenuItem onClick={rename}>Rename</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem onClick={duplicate}>Duplicate</MenuItem>
  <MenuSeparator />
  <MenuItem variant="danger" onClick={remove}>Delete</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

props.name: trigger
props.description: Element that opens the menu as a dropdown (e.g. `<Button>Actions</Button>`). Without it, the menu renders inline.

props.name: side
props.description: Side of the trigger to show the dropdown

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the dropdown's open state changes

entries.name: MenuItem
entries.description: An action in a `Menu`: a `<button role="menuitem">`. In a dropdown, choosing it closes the menu.

entries.name: MenuSeparator
entries.description: A divider between groups of `MenuItem`s.

entries.name: MenuLabel
entries.description: A non-interactive heading for a group of `MenuItem`s.

entries.name: CommandPalette
entries.description: A modal, searchable command list (the "Command-K" pattern). Typing filters `items` by label, arrow keys move, Enter runs the highlighted command and closes. Opening it is up to you (for example on Cmd/Ctrl+K); it calls `onClose` on Escape, an outside click or after a command runs.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Callback when the palette should close

entries.name: CommandItem
entries.description: A command in a `CommandPalette`.

props.name: label
props.description: Text shown and matched by the search

props.name: group
props.description: Heading to group the command under; groups appear in order of first use

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Runs when the command is chosen; the palette then calls `onClose`

entries.name: ToastProvider
entries.description:
Shows the toasts created with `useToast()`; wrap your app in it once.

Built on Base UI. The viewport is a persistent `aria-live` region, so screen readers announce each toast as it is added; `error` toasts are announced assertively (`role="alert"`). Auto-dismiss timers pause while the pointer is over the stack, while it has keyboard focus (F6 jumps to it) and while the window is in the background.

props.name: children
props.description: Your app, or the part of it that shows toasts

entries.name: useToast
entries.description: Shows toasts from anywhere inside a `ToastProvider`. Returns `toast({message, variant, duration})`, which returns the toast's id, and `dismiss(id)`. Throws outside a `ToastProvider`.

entries.name: ToastData
entries.description: A toast, as passed to `toast()` (without `id`).

props.name: variant
props.description: Color and urgency; `error` toasts are announced assertively. Defaults to `'info'`.

props.name: duration
props.description: Milliseconds before it closes itself. Defaults to 5000; `0` or `Infinity` keeps it open until dismissed.

entries.name: Stepper
entries.description: Progress through a multi-step flow. Steps before `activeStep` show as completed, the active one gets `aria-current="step"`. It only displays the steps; moving between them is up to you.
examples:
```tsx
<Stepper activeStep={1}>
  <Step label="Account" />
  <Step label="Profile" description="Tell us about you" />
  <Step label="Confirm" />
</Stepper>
```

props.name: completedLabel
props.description: Text announced to screen readers for completed steps, whose indicator shows only a check mark.

entries.name: Step
entries.description: One step of a `Stepper`. Its number and state come from the Stepper.

props.name: completedLabel
props.description: Text announced to screen readers for a completed step

entries.name: PricingTable
entries.description: A responsive row of `PricingCard`s, one per plan. Columns wrap onto more rows on narrow screens.
examples:
```tsx
<PricingTable>
  <PricingCard>
    <PricingCardHeader>Free</PricingCardHeader>
    <PricingCardPrice amount="$0" period="/month" />
    <PricingCardFeatures>
      <PricingCardFeature>1 project</PricingCardFeature>
      <PricingCardFeature included={false}>Custom domains</PricingCardFeature>
    </PricingCardFeatures>
    <PricingCardFooter><Button variant="outline" expanded>Start free</Button></PricingCardFooter>
  </PricingCard>
  <PricingCard featured>
    <PricingCardHeader>Pro</PricingCardHeader>
    <PricingCardPrice amount="$29" period="/month" />
    <PricingCardFeatures>
      <PricingCardFeature>Unlimited projects</PricingCardFeature>
      <PricingCardFeature>Custom domains</PricingCardFeature>
    </PricingCardFeatures>
    <PricingCardFooter><Button expanded>Upgrade</Button></PricingCardFooter>
  </PricingCard>
</PricingTable>
```

props.name: columns
props.description: Number of columns (auto-fits to content by default)

entries.name: PricingCard
entries.description: One plan in a `PricingTable`; `featured` highlights it.

props.name: featured
props.description: Whether this is the highlighted/recommended plan

entries.name: PricingCardHeader
entries.description: The plan name at the top of a `PricingCard`.

entries.name: PricingCardPrice
entries.description: The price of a `PricingCard`, with an optional billing period.

entries.name: PricingCardFeatures
entries.description: The feature list of a `PricingCard`, a `<ul>` of `PricingCardFeature`s.

entries.name: PricingCardFeature
entries.description: One feature of a plan, with a check mark, or a cross when `included={false}` (announced with `excludedLabel`).

props.name: excludedLabel
props.description: Text announced to screen readers before an excluded feature, whose cross mark is decorative

entries.name: PricingCardFooter
entries.description: The call to action at the bottom of a `PricingCard`.

entries.name: breakpoints
entries.description: Minimum viewport widths, in px, of the breakpoints used by responsive props (`{base, sm, md, lg, xl}`) and `Show`.
entries.signature: { readonly sm: 640; readonly md: 768; readonly lg: 1024; readonly xl: 1280; }

entries.name: Breakpoint
entries.description: A breakpoint name: `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl'`.

entries.name: ResponsiveValue
entries.description: A prop value that can change with screen width: a single value, or an object keyed by breakpoint (`{base: 'sm', md: 'lg'}`), where each key applies from that breakpoint up.
entries.signature: type ResponsiveValue<T> = T | {base?: T; sm?: T; md?: T; lg?: T; xl?: T}
